---
title: "Try the Shiny tools in your browser"
description: >
  The package's six Shiny tools, running in your browser with webR: no R to install, and
  your data never leaves your computer.
---

[![CRAN downloads](https://cranlogs.r-pkg.org/badges/NetSimR)](https://cran.r-project.org/package=NetSimR)
[![Total downloads](https://cranlogs.r-pkg.org/badges/grand-total/NetSimR)](https://cran.r-project.org/package=NetSimR)

The six Shiny tools of NetSimR run right here, in your browser, with
[webR](https://docs.r-wasm.org/webr/latest/), R compiled to WebAssembly, and
[shinylive](https://posit-dev.github.io/r-shinylive/). Nothing to install.

```{=html}

    <h2 id="private">Your data never leaves your computer</h2>
    <p>The tools run inside your browser: R itself is downloaded to the page and does the work there. ## The six Shiny tools
```

```{=html}
<style>
.netsimr-tools { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(16rem, 1fr)); gap: 1rem; margin: 1.5rem 0; }
.netsimr-tool { border: 1px solid var(--bs-border-color); border-radius: 0.75rem; padding: 1rem 1.1rem; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.5rem; }
.netsimr-tool h3 { font-size: 1.1rem; margin: 0; }
.netsimr-tool-kind { display: block; font-size: 0.85rem; font-weight: 500; color: var(--bs-secondary-color); margin-top: 0.2rem; }
.netsimr-tool p { margin: 0; flex: 1; }
.netsimr-tool a.btn { align-self: flex-start; }
</style>
<div class="netsimr-tools">
  <div class="netsimr-tool">
    <h3>NetSimulator <span class="netsimr-tool-kind">Claims &amp; reinsurance simulator</span></h3>
    <p>Frequency-severity simulation with Pareto tails, caps and reinsurance layers, with return periods, run comparison and a report.</p>
    <a class="btn btn-primary" href="../apps/simulator/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Open NetSimulator</a>
  </div>
  <div class="netsimr-tool">
    <h3>NetDisFit <span class="netsimr-tool-kind">Distribution fitting</span></h3>
    <p>Fit claim counts and sizes, including claims above a reporting threshold or at their policy limits; compare the fits with Q-Q, P-P and Hill plots and their tail expectations, and send them to the simulator and the reinsurance pricing tool, with a report.</p>
    <a class="btn btn-primary" href="../apps/distribution/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Open NetDisFit</a>
  </div>
  <div class="netsimr-tool">
    <h3>NetGLM <span class="netsimr-tool-kind">GLM fitting</span></h3>
    <p>Fit generalised linear models to a CSV or Excel file, with splines and bands; let stepwise selection or the lasso suggest the terms, test them on held-out rows, and download the rate table and a report.</p>
    <a class="btn btn-primary" href="../apps/glm/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Open NetGLM</a>
  </div>
  <div class="netsimr-tool">
    <h3>NetReserve <span class="netsimr-tool-kind">Claims reserving</span></h3>
    <p>The chain ladder with Mack's standard errors, Bornhuetter-Ferguson, Cape Cod, the bootstrap and the Munich chain ladder, with discounting and the risk adjustment for IFRS 17 and Solvency II, and a report.</p>
    <a class="btn btn-primary" href="../apps/reserving/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Open NetReserve</a>
  </div>
  <div class="netsimr-tool">
    <h3>NetTreaty <span class="netsimr-tool-kind">Reinsurance pricing</span></h3>
    <p>Price an excess of loss layer with the burning cost, a Pareto model and exposure curves, blend them, and compare quota share, surplus, excess of loss and stop loss programmes by their cost and the capital they save, with a report.</p>
    <a class="btn btn-primary" href="../apps/reinsurance/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Open NetTreaty</a>
  </div>
  <div class="netsimr-tool">
    <h3>NetCapital <span class="netsimr-tool-kind">Portfolio capital</span></h3>
    <p>Join lines of business with a Gaussian or t copula: VaR, TVaR, diversification and each line's capital, beside the Solvency II standard formula.</p>
    <a class="btn btn-primary" href="../apps/portfolio/" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Open NetCapital</a>
  </div>
</div>
```

New to the tools? [A worked example](worked-example.html) runs each of them on the package's
example data, with the report it writes.

## Your data stays on your computer

Claims, policies and triangles are confidential, so this is worth being exact about.

- **Where the work is done.** A tool's page downloads R and the packages it needs, and runs them in
  your browser. The file you choose is handed by the browser to that R, in the page's memory. The
  fits, simulations and charts are made there.
- **What is sent: nothing of yours.** The website is static pages on GitHub Pages. There is no
  server behind it that runs code or could keep a file, so there is nowhere for a file to go.
- **What the page does fetch.** Downloads only: R, its packages and their files, from this website
  and from [the repository of webR](https://repo.r-wasm.org/). None of these requests carries
  anything from your files or your results. The tools bring their own fonts and icons, so a page
  asks no other server for anything.
- **The one thing reported: that a page was visited.** The website counts page visits with
  [GoatCounter](https://www.goatcounter.com/): the address of the page, where the visit came
  from, the kind of browser, the size of its screen and the country, without cookies or personal
  data. Nothing you upload, type or compute is part of it.
- **What you save stays with you.** Reports, settings files and CSV or Excel downloads are written
  by your browser to your own computer. Closing the tab ends the session and clears its memory.
- **How it was checked.** In November 2026 a file of claims with marked values was opened and
  fitted in NetDisFit on this website, while the browser logged every request it made to the
  network. The file's name and its values were in none of them.
- **In R, the same holds.** Installed from CRAN, the tools run in R on your own computer, need no
  internet connection and make no request to any other server, and count nothing. The GLM tool's
  database source connects only to the database you name. If your company's rules exclude any
  web tool, this is the way to use them.

The package's code, and the workflow that builds this website from it, are public on
[GitHub](https://github.com/NetSimAnalytics/NetSimR).

## Good to know

- **The first start takes a little while**: the browser downloads R and the packages, a few tens of
  megabytes. Later starts are quicker, as the browser keeps them.
- **Closing the tab ends the session**: save the settings of a tool to come back to it.
- **Some things need R on your computer**: the simulator's parallel workers, and the GLM tool's
  database connections, are not available in the browser. Large simulations also run faster in R.
- A recent version of Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari is needed.

## In R

The same tools run from R, after installing the package from CRAN or, for the newest version, from
GitHub:

```r
install.packages("NetSimR")
# or: remotes::install_github("NetSimAnalytics/NetSimR")
library(NetSimR)
run_shiny_simulator()
run_shiny_distribution_fitting_tool()
run_shiny_glm_fitting_tool()
run_shiny_reserving_tool()
run_shiny_reinsurance_pricing_tool()
run_shiny_portfolio_tool()
```
